fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Access Drive; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions on the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with posts or reflectors on both sides to help responders locate the turn-in at night or in low visibility.
• Trim tree branches overhanging the driveway to maintain clearance for fire apparatus and ladder trucks.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and debris so responding units can reach the residence without obstruction.
• Identify and mark an alternate foot access route to the rear of the property for responders who cannot reach it by vehicle.
• Cut back dense vegetation along both sides of the driveway so responders can move along the drive and turn apparatus if needed.
• Trim shrubs and low branches away from the exterior walls and roof edges of both the main residence and the detached structure.
• Post the property address on the detached structure if it is not already visible, so responders can identify it as a secondary building on arrival.
• Keep a gate or gap in any rear fencing unlocked or marked so responders on foot can access the back of the property without delay.
• Designate and keep clear a flat, firm staging area near the residence where apparatus can park and crews can work without repositioning vehicles.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Vegetation Near Structure; Open Terrain; Structure Cluster; Long Driveway; Vegetation Along Driveway; Scattered Shrubs; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Ground Vegetation; Single Access Route; Mixed Vegetation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees within the scattered clusters closest to the structures to reduce the amount of burnable material directly near buildings.
• Remove or cut back shrubs that are growing immediately against any of the structures in the cluster.
• Trim overhanging branches along the full length of the driveway to keep it passable for vehicles.
• Cut back vegetation growing along the sides of the driveway so a vehicle can pass through without contact.
• Keep the single access route clear of fallen branches, overgrown shrubs, and any debris that could block entry or exit.
• Thin ground vegetation beneath and between tree clusters near the structures to reduce the amount of burnable material at ground level.
• Separate any shrubs or ground cover that forms a continuous line from open terrain toward the structures.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from around the base of trees located near the buildings.
• Keep the areas between structures in the cluster clear of accumulated leaves, dry grass, and loose plant debris.
• Maintain the existing open areas between vegetation and structures by preventing shrub or tree regrowth into those gaps.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so that emergency vehicles can locate and use the access route without delay.
